title: EC2 and EBS: when you own the machine
outcome: Explain instance lifecycle, disk persistence, process supervision, and the responsibilities EC2 leaves with you.
useCase: Understanding existing VM deployments and choosing compute ownership.
drawbacks: Patching, configuration drift, and recovery remain your work.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: A machine is replaceable only if its important state is accounted for.

trace.title: Image and instance
trace.detail: EC2 gives you virtual machines. You choose an image, instance capacity, network, identity, and storage. You still own operating-system patching, process configuration, application deployment, and much of the recovery plan.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Boot image → inject configuration/identity → start supervised process → health check → receive traffic. Replacement should recreate the application from its artifact/configuration, not depend on manual edits left on the old machine.

Scale to two instances and follow an upload/read. If only one instance has the file, the storage boundary is wrong for that architecture.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A manually repaired server becomes hard to reproduce. A successful reboot is not a tested restore. Local logs disappear with the machine if not collected.
